project:2.en: Deep in the archive I found a folder marked VOID. Inside: blueprints, budget sheets, a team list of thirty names. All crossed out. Ali leaned over my shoulder. 'That is the *project* Zero shut down five years ago,' she whispered. 'Nobody talks about it. Nobody who knows is still around.'
project:2.cnHint: 我在档案室发现了一个被零点中止的____，所有知情者都消失了。
project:2.hook: My own name was typed at the bottom of the team list.
project:2.line: 'The *project* was buried — but the data never was.'

record:2.en: The disc was ancient, the kind no one used anymore. Grey Crow held it up to the blue emergency light. 'This is a *record* of every signal Zero ever broadcast,' he said quietly. 'Every frequency, every date.' In the wrong hands it was a map. In the right hands it was a weapon.
record:2.cnHint: 灰鸦找到一张____，上面存有零点所有广播信号的历史。
record:2.hook: Someone had already copied two tracks — and the copies were missing.
record:2.line: 'This *record* proves Zero has been watching us for years.'

regular:2.en: Ali checked the log and frowned. 'Look at the timestamps.' I leaned in. Every seventy-two hours, without fail, a small data packet left this terminal — quiet, clean, invisible to a *regular* scan. Someone inside the building had been feeding information out for months, hiding in plain sight.
regular:2.cnHint: 阿栗发现每隔72小时就有数据包悄悄外传，普通的____扫描根本发现不了。
regular:2.hook: The next packet was scheduled to send in four minutes.
regular:2.line: 'A *regular* scan will miss it — you need deeper access.'

security:2.en: The door to the relay room had no handle, only a flat panel that read AUTHORIZED ONLY. Grey Crow crouched beside it and traced a thin wire running along the baseboard. 'They upgraded the *security* after the last breach,' he murmured. 'But they forgot one thing.' He pressed the wire and the panel went dark.
security:2.cnHint: 中继室的____系统被升级过，但灰鸦发现了一个被遗忘的漏洞。
security:2.hook: The door sighed open — and cold air poured out like a held breath.
security:2.line: 'Their *security* is tight — except for this one old wire.'

review:2.en: The archive room smelled of old rain and burnt wire. I spread the signal logs across the table for a *review* — three nights of blackouts, each one erasing a different city block. Grey Crow had marked certain entries in red. The pattern was not random.
review:2.cnHint: 我在档案室对信号记录进行____，发现断电并非偶然。
review:2.hook: The last red mark pointed straight to our building.
review:2.line: 'Do a careful *review* — every erased block hides a name.'

ahead:2.en: Ali pulled me into a side tunnel beneath the power grid. The smell of burning cables was close. She pressed a small screen into my hand — a map with a blinking red dot moving *ahead* of us, two corridors away. Someone knew exactly where we were going.
ahead:2.cnHint: 阿栗给我看地图，那个红点在我们____方向移动，对方似乎掌握了我们的路线。
ahead:2.hook: The dot stopped — right where the tunnel ended.
ahead:2.line: 'They are *ahead* of us — change the route now.'

cheap:2.en: Zero left a data chip taped under the fire-exit sign. The chip itself was a *cheap* piece of grey plastic, the kind sold in street markets for almost nothing. But the file inside listed every hidden relay tower in Harbor City. I felt the weight of it change.
cheap:2.cnHint: 零点留下的芯片外观____，里面却藏着整座城市的秘密中继站名单。
cheap:2.hook: One tower on the list had today's date stamped in red.
cheap:2.line: 'Don't trust anything *cheap* — the real cost is always hidden.'

critical:2.en: Grey Crow's voice came through a burst of static. 'The south relay,' he said, 'is *critical* — if it goes dark, every encrypted channel in Harbor City collapses at once.' I looked at the power meter on the wall. The needle was already falling toward zero.
critical:2.cnHint: 灰鸦告诉我南部中继站处于____时刻，一旦断电整个城市的加密频道都会崩溃。
critical:2.hook: The needle touched zero, and the room went silent.
critical:2.line: 'That relay is *critical* — guard it until I arrive.'

motivate:2.en: I found a short message scratched onto the inside of a locker door: 'What can *motivate* a person to erase their own name from every city record?' Below it, a small arrow pointed to a folded page. Ali read it first and said nothing for a long moment.
motivate:2.cnHint: 储物柜里的留言提出了一个问题：什么能____一个人删去自己在城市里的全部记录？
motivate:2.hook: Ali finally turned the page over — her own name was on it.
motivate:2.line: 'Tell me what can *motivate* someone to disappear so completely.'

charge:2.en: The station guard met us at the gate. He said the city would *charge* anyone caught near the grid a heavy fine, enough to clear out a month's wages. Ali showed him a blank card and smiled. He stepped aside without another word. That card was not blank at all.
charge:2.cnHint: 守卫说靠近电网会被____高额罚款，但阿栗出示的那张卡让他立刻让路。
charge:2.hook: I needed to know what code that card was carrying.
charge:2.line: 'They will *charge* us the moment we cross that line.'

complex:2.en: The sub-station map looked *complex* at first — a web of coloured lines crossing in ways that made no sense. Then Ali turned it ninety degrees and the pattern resolved into a single word written in circuit paths. Grey Crow had hidden a message inside the wiring diagram itself.
complex:2.cnHint: 变电站地图看起来____难懂，但转个方向后，电路路径里藏着一个单词。
complex:2.hook: The word spelled out the name of someone I trusted.
complex:2.line: 'The layout is *complex* — but the answer is already inside it.'

itself:2.en: The blackout signal did not come from outside the city. Grey Crow's trace showed it originating from the grid *itself* — a loop buried so deep that the system had been switching itself off on a timer for weeks. No intruder. The city's own network was the threat.
itself:2.cnHint: 停电信号来自电网____，城市的网络系统一直在按计时器关闭自己。
itself:2.hook: Someone had written that timer into the grid on day one.
itself:2.line: 'The danger is in the grid *itself* — we built the trap.'

whatever:2.en: The blackout hit at midnight. Every screen in the archive room went dark. I swept my light across the shelves — files, drives, old paper logs. Grey Crow had said, '*Whatever* signal you find in there, copy it and run.' I found a small drive taped behind a loose panel. It was still warm.
whatever:2.cnHint: 停电后，我在档案室找到了一个被藏起来的小装置，灰鸦曾告诉我无论找到____，都要立刻带走。
whatever:2.hook: The drive held one file — and it had my name on it.
whatever:2.line: '*Whatever* you find behind that panel, do not open it here.'

predict:2.en: Ali spread the old city maps across the floor of the signal room. 'Someone used these to *predict* where the blackouts would hit next,' she said, tracing ink marks between three districts. The pattern was not random. It was a countdown, drawn weeks before the power died tonight.
predict:2.cnHint: 阿里发现有人早已用旧地图____出了断电的顺序，这绝非巧合。
predict:2.hook: The next mark on the map pointed straight to our building.
predict:2.line: 'They used this map to *predict* every blackout — weeks in advance.'

road:2.en: I stepped out into the wet street. The *road* below the overpass was empty except for one blinking yellow light at the far end. Grey Crow had told me to follow the light. Somewhere under the neon puddles, a wire ran from this block to the city's dead core. I started walking.
road:2.cnHint: 停电的夜里，我独自走上那条____，追随着远处唯一一盏闪烁的黄灯。
road:2.hook: Halfway down, the yellow light went out.
road:2.line: 'Stay on this *road* — it leads to the signal source.'

solution:2.en: Zero's voice cut through the static on my earpiece. 'There is no clean *solution* to a locked cipher like this,' he said, almost amused. 'You either burn the key or burn the building.' I stared at the locked terminal. Ali was already pulling a secondary cable from the wall behind it.
solution:2.cnHint: 零点冷冷地说，对付这种加密终端没有什么好的____，但阿里已经悄悄行动了。
solution:2.hook: Ali's hands stopped — the cable was already cut.
solution:2.line: 'There is no easy *solution*; someone got here before us.'

total:2.en: Ali ran the diagnostics twice. The result was the same both times. '*Total* signal loss across the eastern grid,' she read out, her voice flat. Not a partial failure — every node, every relay, every backup channel: silent. Someone had not just cut the power. They had erased the network itself.
total:2.cnHint: 阿里的检测显示东区信号____中断，不是局部故障，而是彻底消失。
total:2.hook: One node, deep underground, was still alive.
total:2.line: '*Total* blackout — every single channel is gone.'

fail:2.en: The decryption timer hit zero. Nothing opened. Grey Crow watched the screen go blank and said nothing for a long moment. 'Every method we try will *fail* as long as the root key is missing,' he finally said. He turned to me slowly. 'And you are the only one who has touched the root drive.'
fail:2.cnHint: 解密再次____，灰鸦转向我，眼神意味深长。
fail:2.hook: His eyes told me I was no longer just a witness.
fail:2.line: 'Every attempt will *fail* until we recover the root key.'

function:2.en: The old terminal in the basement still had power. I pressed the switch and one pale screen came on. Most icons were dead, but one small program still had *function*. It was a listener — passive, invisible, recording every signal that passed through the building. It had been running for six years without anyone knowing.
function:2.cnHint: 地下室那台旧终端的一个程序仍然有____，它一直在悄悄记录着所有信号。
function:2.hook: The log showed a signal sent from my own floor — tonight.
function:2.line: 'This one program still has *function* — it recorded everything.'

method:2.en: Zero left a message burned onto a strip of paper tucked inside the fuse box. Three words and a number. I had seen this *method* before — it was how operatives passed orders when all digital channels were watched. The paper was still warm. He had been here minutes ago, maybe less.
method:2.cnHint: 零点用一种老式____传递信息——一张夹在保险丝盒里的纸条，字迹还带着余温。
method:2.hook: The number on the paper matched the room above my head.
method:2.line: 'This *method* means he knew every digital line was watched.'

join:2.en: Deep in the server tunnels beneath Harbor City, I found two severed cables. Someone had tried to *join* them with copper wire — a crude fix, but deliberate. This was not an accident. The splice carried a faint signal, a rhythm like breathing. Ali had warned me about hidden networks. Now I believed her.
join:2.cnHint: 调查员在隧道里发现被切断的电缆被人用铜线____在一起，传出神秘信号。
join:2.hook: The signal pulsed once, then spelled a name.
join:2.line: 'Someone tried to *join* these cables — and they knew exactly which ones.'

significant:2.en: Ali slid a data chip across the broken table. 'Look at the timestamp,' she said. I looked. The file was written at the exact moment the city grid went dark. That was no accident — it was too *significant* a match. Someone had killed the lights on purpose, and this chip proved it.
significant:2.cnHint: 阿里发现一个文件的时间戳与全城断电时刻完全吻合，这一发现极为____。
significant:2.hook: The chip also contained a second file — locked, and addressed to me.
significant:2.line: 'That timestamp is too *significant* to ignore — someone planned this.'

step:2.en: The archive room was dark. I *stepped* carefully between rows of old data towers, each one cold and silent. On the floor, a line of faint boot prints led toward the back wall. Whoever had been here moved with purpose. They had found something. I followed the trail, breath held tight.
step:2.cnHint: 调查员____入黑暗的档案室，追踪地板上一行神秘的靴印。
step:2.hook: The last boot print stopped — right in front of a sealed door.
step:2.line: '*Step* carefully — the floor sensors are still active.'

unique:2.en: Grey Crow handed me a fragment of printed paper — rare in 2099. The typeface was *unique*: no machine in Harbor City used that exact letter shape. It had been printed on a device that did not officially exist. I pressed the paper flat. Someone was operating outside every known network, every known rule.
unique:2.cnHint: 灰鸦交给调查员一张纸质碎片，上面的字体____，来自一台官方记录中根本不存在的设备。
unique:2.hook: On the back, in pencil, were the coordinates of a place I knew well.
unique:2.line: 'This typeface is *unique* — no registered press in the city made it.'

inside:2.en: The relay box looked ordinary from the street. But *inside*, the wiring had been replaced entirely — clean work, professional. Someone had rebuilt it from scratch and hidden a transmitter no larger than a coin among the circuits. It had been broadcasting for days. No one had noticed. Until now.
inside:2.cnHint: 外表普通的中继箱____被人彻底改装，藏着一枚持续广播数日的微型发射器。
inside:2.line: 'Look *inside* — someone rebuilt this whole box from scratch.'

majority:2.en: I pulled up the city-wide outage report. The *majority* of blackouts clustered in one district: the old port. Not random failures. A pattern, deliberate and tight. Zero had been cutting power block by block, testing response times, mapping the gaps. He was not causing chaos. He was running a rehearsal.
majority:2.cnHint: 停电报告显示，____的断电事故集中在旧港区，这绝非随机故障，而是零点精心策划的演练。
majority:2.hook: The next block on the pattern was the police communications hub.
majority:2.line: 'The *majority* of cuts are in the port — that is not random.'

notice:2.en: Pinned to the door of the empty safe house was a single sheet of paper. It was an official *notice* — building inspection, routine maintenance — but the date was wrong by exactly one year. A signal. Grey Crow had left it. The false date was a code that told me when to move, and where.
notice:2.cnHint: 灰鸦在废弃据点门上贴了一张日期故意写错的____，其中藏着行动时间和地点的暗语。
notice:2.hook: I checked my watch — the coded time was forty minutes from now.
notice:2.line: 'Read that *notice* again — the date is the message.'

taste:2.en: Ali passed me a small flask. 'Drink,' she said. 'It helps you think.' The liquid had a sharp, metallic *taste* — not water, not anything sold in stores. She watched my face. 'Grey Crow's formula,' she added quietly. My vision sharpened. The room's hidden signals rose like sound, clear and cold and waiting.
taste:2.cnHint: 阿里递给调查员一瓶灰鸦配制的液体，那股金属____令他的感知骤然增强，隐藏信号变得清晰可辨。
taste:2.hook: On the wall, the coded graffiti began to make sense at last.
taste:2.line: 'The *taste* is strange, I know — but it opens the signals up.'

differ:2.en: The dead server room smelled of burnt wire. Ali pulled two data chips from the wreckage and held them under her torch. 'These *differ* in one small way,' she said. One edge had a tiny notch. The other was smooth. Someone had swapped the original.
differ:2.cnHint: 阿栗在废弃机房里发现两块芯片，它们之间有一处微妙的____。
differ:2.hook: Only one chip held the truth — but which one?
differ:2.line: 'These *differ* in one small way, and that way matters.'

shape:2.en: The blackout had lasted six hours. In the flooded basement of Tower Nine, I found it pressed into the wet concrete: a *shape* like a crow's wing, small and sharp. Grey Crow had been here. He left this mark on purpose. Every line meant something.
shape:2.cnHint: 停电后，我在积水地下室的混凝土上发现了一个特殊的____。
shape:2.hook: The mark was still fresh — he could not be far.
shape:2.line: 'That *shape* is a message — read it before the water rises.'

twice:2.en: Ali had visited the signal tower *twice* before the blackout. The first time she found nothing. The second time she did not come back alone. Now, standing at the locked door, I counted two sets of boot prints in the dust. She had brought someone here.
twice:2.cnHint: 停电前，阿栗曾____到访信号塔，第二次她并非独自离开。
twice:2.hook: The second set of prints was too large to be hers.
twice:2.line: 'I went there *twice* — and the second visit changed everything.'

aspect:2.en: Zero's broadcast cut through every screen in the city for four seconds. I recorded it and studied each *aspect* of the signal: its timing, its pitch, its hidden gaps. One gap repeated. It was not noise. It was a name, spelled in broken pulses. My name.
aspect:2.cnHint: 零点的广播信号有一个____让我震惊——其中藏着我自己的名字。
aspect:2.hook: If Zero knew my name, he had known me long before tonight.
aspect:2.line: 'Every *aspect* of that signal was aimed at you — only you.'

currently:2.en: Grey Crow's map showed nine safe houses across Harbor City. Eight were burned or sealed. '*Currently* only one remains open,' the note read, in his tight, careful handwriting. Below the address he had drawn a small arrow pointing down. Under the floor, then. Not inside.
currently:2.cnHint: 灰鸦的地图显示，九处藏身点中____只剩一处可用。
currently:2.hook: The arrow pointed down — into something the map refused to name.
currently:2.line: '*Currently* one door is open, and it will not stay open long.'

decrease:2.en: The city's power grid was failing in stages. Ali watched the numbers on her monitor *decrease* — block by block, district by district, light by light. At this rate, the whole eastern grid would be dark in eleven minutes. Whatever we needed to find, we had to find it now.
decrease:2.cnHint: 阿栗盯着屏幕，眼看着电网数值不断____，时间所剩无几。
decrease:2.hook: Eleven minutes — and the thing we feared lived in the dark.
decrease:2.line: 'Watch the numbers *decrease* — when they hit zero, we lose everything.'

possibility:2.en: I spread Grey Crow's notes across the floor of the old relay station. Three suspects. Three different motives. But one detail kept pulling at me: all three had been in this building the night of the first blackout. The *possibility* that they had worked together felt suddenly very real.
possibility:2.cnHint: 我整理灰鸦的笔记，发现三名嫌疑人也许共谋的____越来越大。
possibility:2.hook: If they were a team, I had been chasing shadows from the start.
possibility:2.line: 'The *possibility* that they planned this together — can you rule it out?'

crucial:2.en: The chip contained only one file. Inside was a timestamp and four words. Ali stared at them. 'This is *crucial*,' she said quietly. The timestamp matched the exact moment of the city's first blackout two years ago. Someone had predicted the darkness before it ever came.
crucial:2.cnHint: 芯片里只有一个文件，阿栗说其中的时间戳____无比——它早于那场停电整整两年。
crucial:2.hook: Someone had written the date of our disaster before it happened.
crucial:2.line: 'This timestamp is *crucial* — it means someone planned the blackout years ago.'

enormous:2.en: The blackout had lasted three hours. Ali led me down to the server vault beneath the old port. The door was open — wrong. Inside, an *enormous* machine filled the whole room, its casing cracked, its cooling fans still spinning in the dark. Someone had powered it on just before the grid died.
enormous:2.cnHint: 阿栗带我找到地下机房，发现一台____的机器正在运转。
enormous:2.hook: The screen blinked once, then showed my name.
enormous:2.line: 'That *enormous* thing was never on the city grid — it runs alone.'

pet:2.en: Grey Crow kept an old contact on Level 9, a data broker who owned a small white cat. The cat — his only *pet* — sat on a locked drawer. Grey Crow said the man never left that cat alone with strangers. The drawer was open. The man was gone.
pet:2.cnHint: 那个数据掮客的____守着一个被打开的抽屉，人却不见了。
pet:2.hook: Inside the drawer: a folded note with my frequency on it.
pet:2.line: 'He loved that *pet* more than money — leaving her here means he had no choice.'

restaurant:2.en: The meet was set for a dim noodle *restaurant* on Pier 7, the kind of place where the menu was written in chalk and changed every hour. Ali slid a napkin across the table. On it, three numbers. I looked up — the cook behind the counter was already watching me.
restaurant:2.cnHint: 阿栗在码头的____里递给我一张写有数字的纸巾。
restaurant:2.hook: The chalk menu now read: 'Leave. Now.'
restaurant:2.line: 'Every *restaurant* on this pier reports to Zero — we have two minutes.'

driver:2.en: The cargo tram had no passengers, only crates. The *driver* — a thin woman with a silver earpiece — did not look back once. Ali whispered that she had been on the same route every night of the blackout week. Under her seat I spotted a small red case that did not belong.
driver:2.cnHint: 那位____每晚都走同一条路线，座位下藏着一个可疑的红色箱子。
driver:2.hook: Her earpiece crackled, and she finally turned to look at us.
driver:2.line: 'A *driver* who never changes routes during a crisis is following orders, not habit.'

dream:2.en: The file was labelled simply: DREAM. Grey Crow said it was Zero's earliest project — a plan to rewrite the city's broadcast language so that every *dream* a citizen described in public could be logged and searched. The file was dated fifteen years ago. Some pages were already law.
dream:2.cnHint: 灰鸦让我看零点的早期计划，一个将市民的____变成监控数据的系统。
dream:2.hook: The last page listed three names — mine was the third.
dream:2.line: 'They called it a *dream*, but it was always a trap.'

consumer:2.en: Zero's network did not sell data — it gave it away free. Grey Crow explained the model: every *consumer* who accepted the free signal also accepted a hidden listener buried in the stream. Forty million users. Forty million open ears. I stared at the map. Harbor City glowed solid red.
consumer:2.cnHint: 灰鸦解释零点的计划——每个免费信号的____都成了被监听的对象。
consumer:2.hook: One node on the map pulsed faster than the rest — my block.
consumer:2.line: 'Every *consumer* thinks they got something free — no one ever does.'

interesting:2.en: Ali pulled up the access log and went quiet. 'That is *interesting*,' she said at last. Someone had entered the archive during the blackout using a pass that had been cancelled two years ago. The record showed four minutes of access, then a clean exit. Nothing was taken. Something was left.
interesting:2.cnHint: 阿栗查看访问记录，发现一件____的事：一张作废的通行证在断电期间被使用了。
interesting:2.hook: The file that was left had no author and no date.
interesting:2.line: '*Interesting* — the old pass works again only when the main grid is down.'

grade:2.en: The contraband broadcast chips were sorted by *grade*: A for city-wide range, B for single district, C for personal use only. The crate Ali found held nothing but grade-A chips — enough to reach every receiver in Harbor City at once. There were two hundred of them. All were already charged.
grade:2.cnHint: 阿栗发现的箱子里装满最高____的广播芯片，足以覆盖全城。
grade:2.hook: The transmission timer on the top chip read: forty minutes.

rule:2.en: Deep inside the dead archive tower, I found a cracked tablet. Its screen still glowed. On it: a single document titled HARBOR CITY OPERATING PROTOCOL. Page one read, 'Under Zero's *rule*, all broadcast channels belong to the State.' Grey Crow had warned me this document existed. Now I held it.
rule:2.cnHint: 我在废弃档案塔里发现了一份文件，揭示了零点对这座城市的____。
rule:2.hook: Someone had already circled page one in red.
rule:2.line: 'Under his *rule*, even silence is a crime,' Grey Crow said.

plant:2.en: Ali led me down a fire escape to a flooded basement. Thick green vines covered every wall — an impossible *plant* thriving without light. Woven into its stems were tiny transmitters, still pulsing. Someone had grown a living antenna. The signal it carried was addressed to me.
plant:2.cnHint: 阿栗带我发现了一株奇异的____，它的茎里藏着正在运作的信号发射器。
plant:2.hook: The address on the signal was my childhood home.
plant:2.line: 'This *plant* has been broadcasting for six years,' Ali whispered.

doctor:2.en: The sealed room smelled of chemicals. On the steel table lay a single notebook, its cover stamped DR. VOSS — FINAL REPORT. Inside, equations I could not read. But the last page was plain language: 'The signal does not carry data. It carries orders.' I looked for the *doctor*. The chair was still warm.
doctor:2.cnHint: 我找到了一位____留下的最终报告，最后一页用普通语言写着令人不安的结论。
doctor:2.hook: The notebook's final line had been torn away cleanly.
doctor:2.line: 'The *doctor* knew too much and stayed too long,' Zero's voice said.

economy:2.en: Grey Crow spread a map across the wet floor. Red lines connected every power station in Harbor City. 'This is not about politics,' he said. 'It is about the *economy* — whoever controls the grid controls every transaction, every debt, every life.' The blackout tonight was not an accident. It was a message.
economy:2.cnHint: 灰鸦向我展示了一张地图，解释这场停电其实是一场关于____的战争。
economy:2.hook: His finger stopped on the station closest to us.
economy:2.line: 'Control the grid, control the *economy*, control the people,' Grey Crow said.

global:2.en: I cracked the broadcast file at last. It was a live feed — not local, not city-wide. The header read: TRANSMISSION REACH — *GLOBAL*. Zero's signal was already leaving Harbor City, spreading across every ocean. Ali grabbed my arm. We had minutes, not hours, before it locked in.
global:2.cnHint: 我破解的广播文件显示，零点的信号传播范围是____性的，已经越出了城市边界。
global:2.hook: The counter on screen read: lock confirmed in 00:04:00.
global:2.line: 'A *global* signal cannot be recalled once it is sent,' Ali said.

leader:2.en: Tucked behind a loose panel in the metro tunnel, I found a photograph. Twelve people stood in a row, faces crossed out one by one in black marker. Only the figure at the centre remained unmarked. Printed below: THE LAST *LEADER* OF THE OLD NETWORK. I recognised the coat. It was Grey Crow's.
leader:2.cnHint: 我在地铁隧道里发现了一张照片，照片中只有一位旧网络的____没有被划掉。
leader:2.hook: Grey Crow had never once mentioned the old network to me.
leader:2.line: 'A *leader* without a name is the hardest one to stop,' Zero said.

scientific:2.en: The lab had been cleared in a hurry — drawers open, drives wiped. One thing remained: a glass case holding a single printed page. The header read HARBOR CITY *SCIENTIFIC* RESEARCH DIVISION — CLASSIFIED. Below it, one line of text: 'The signal rewrites memory.' Ali read it twice, then looked at me with careful eyes.
scientific:2.cnHint: 实验室里唯一留下的文件来自一个____研究部门，上面只有一行令人不安的结论。
scientific:2.hook: Ali asked quietly if I remembered yesterday clearly.
scientific:2.line: '*Scientific* proof means they tested it on someone,' Ali said.

evidence:2.en: The server room was dark except for one blinking light. In the *evidence* left behind — a burned circuit card, three missing files, a boot print in the dust — I read Zero's message clearly. He had been here. He had taken something. And he had left this for me to find.
evidence:2.cnHint: 断电的服务器室里，我在现场的____中发现了零点留下的痕迹。
evidence:2.hook: The boot print matched no one on our team.
evidence:2.line: 'This *evidence* points to someone who wanted to be found,' Grey Crow said.

prefer:2.en: Grey Crow handed me two routes on the cracked map. 'I *prefer* the tunnel under Block Nine,' he said quietly. 'Streets are watched.' Ali shook her head. The rain hammered the roof. I looked at both paths and felt the weight of the choice settle on my chest like cold iron.
prefer:2.cnHint: 灰鸦告诉我他____走地下隧道，但阿栗有不同意见。
prefer:2.hook: Neither route was safe — and someone already knew which one we'd pick.
prefer:2.line: 'I *prefer* to move unseen,' Grey Crow said, folding the map.

interview:2.en: I found the old recording in a dusty cabinet: Grey Crow's *interview* with a city engineer, taped years before the blackout law. The engineer spoke in careful words, but between the lines I heard the truth about Harbor City's grid — who built the kill switch, and why it was never removed.
interview:2.cnHint: 一段旧录音记录了灰鸦对一位工程师的____，其中藏着断电的秘密。
interview:2.hook: The engineer on the tape had vanished six days after recording it.
interview:2.line: 'That *interview* cost him everything,' Ali whispered, pressing stop.

middle:2.en: The signal arrived at midnight, splitting my receiver screen in two. In the *middle* of the noise — between the static and the city's dead broadcast — a single word pulsed in clean code. I wrote it down. Ali leaned over my shoulder, and for a moment neither of us breathed.
middle:2.cnHint: 在两段杂音的____，我从接收器里截获了一个神秘的单词信号。
middle:2.hook: The word meant nothing alone — but it completed Zero's earlier message.
middle:2.line: 'Look at the *middle* frequency,' Ali said. 'It's a pattern.'

standard:2.en: The data packet looked normal at first glance — *standard* compression, standard headers, the kind of file the city network moved ten thousand times a day. But one byte was off. I almost missed it. Grey Crow had told me once: the best traps wear ordinary clothes. This was a trap.
standard:2.cnHint: 那个数据包看起来完全____，但我发现了一个异常的字节。
standard:2.hook: One wrong byte could mean the file was meant to find me, not the other way around.
standard:2.line: '*Standard* format hides the best knives,' Grey Crow said flatly.

subject:2.en: Ali spread the intercepted pages across the floor. Every message Zero had sent this month shared one *subject*: the old lighthouse at the edge of the harbor. I had walked past it a hundred times without a second thought. Now it felt like every word on those pages was pointing at me, waiting.
subject:2.cnHint: 零点这个月所有信息都有同一个____，就是港口边那座灯塔。
subject:2.hook: The lighthouse had been officially empty for thirty years.
subject:2.line: 'The *subject* never changes,' Ali said. 'That's not an accident.'

accept:2.en: Grey Crow pushed the small drive across the table toward me. 'Take it or don't,' he said. 'But if you *accept* it, you own everything on it.' I looked at the drive. The rain outside the window was loud and steady. I knew that picking it up would change the shape of my life.
accept:2.cnHint: 灰鸦要我____那个装有秘密文件的小硬盘，并告诉我这意味着什么。
accept:2.hook: My hand moved before my mind could stop it.
accept:2.line: 'If you *accept* this, there is no quiet way back,' Grey Crow said.

act:2.en: The lights in the archive room came back on for exactly four seconds. In that brief *act* of power — unscheduled, unexplained — every screen lit up and showed the same image: a map of Harbor City with one building circled in red. Then the dark returned, total and heavy, as if nothing had happened.
act:2.cnHint: 停电中有四秒钟突然来电的____，所有屏幕同时显示出一张标记了红圈的地图。
act:2.hook: No one had access to the grid — no one who was still alive.
act:2.line: 'That *act* was a message,' I said. 'Someone is still inside the system.'

decline:2.en: The old market district was dying. Grey Crow spread a map across the wet table and traced the empty blocks with one finger. 'Look at the *decline*,' he said. 'Three years ago, every signal in this grid was alive. Now — silence.' I studied the dead zones. Someone had erased an entire neighborhood from the city's voice.
decline:2.cnHint: 灰鸦向我展示了地图，指出某个区域正经历严重的____，信号全部消失。
decline:2.hook: The silence on the map had a shape — and it spelled a name.
decline:2.line: 'The *decline* started the night the broadcasts went dark.'

extra:2.en: Ali passed me a small drive under the table. 'There is one *extra* file on there,' she whispered, eyes on the door. 'Grey Crow does not know about it.' The rain hammered the roof of the noodle stall. I slipped the drive into my coat. Whatever was on it, someone had gone to great lengths to hide it here.
extra:2.cnHint: 阿栗偷偷给了我一个存储器，说里面有一个____的文件，不让灰鸦知道。
extra:2.hook: The file had no name — only a countdown.
extra:2.line: 'One *extra* copy exists, and you are now holding it.'

income:2.en: The coded graffiti on the wall listed numbers — not prices, but *income* records. Someone was tracking who paid whom across the whole lower district. Grey Crow had told me to look for patterns. I found one. Every figure on the wall pointed back to a single account, and that account belonged to Zero.
income:2.cnHint: 墙上的涂鸦记录着一份____清单，所有数字都指向同一个账户。
income:2.hook: The account had been opened the day I joined the force.
income:2.line: 'His *income* from last month alone could buy half this block.'

medicine:2.en: The package on the doorstep was wrapped in plain grey cloth. Inside: a bottle of *medicine* with no label, and a note in cipher. Ali scanned it fast. 'This compound does not treat any known illness,' she said quietly. 'It treats memory.' My hands went cold. Someone knew what I had been trying to forget.
medicine:2.cnHint: 门口出现了一瓶没有标签的____，阿栗说它的作用是影响记忆。
medicine:2.hook: The note was signed with a symbol I last saw in my own case file.
medicine:2.line: 'This *medicine* does not heal you — it erases you.'

private:2.en: The server room was locked behind three doors. Grey Crow cut the last seal and pushed it open. Inside, one screen still glowed. On it: a *private* channel, live, streaming voices I was not supposed to hear. I recognized one of them. It was my own commander, speaking to Zero in a calm, familiar tone.
private:2.cnHint: 我们闯入了一个服务器房间，发现一个____频道正在直播，传来了熟悉的声音。
private:2.hook: My commander laughed — and used Zero's real name.
private:2.line: 'This is a *private* channel. No record. No trace. That was the deal.'

side:2.en: Ali pulled me to the *side* of the bridge just before the patrol light swept across. We pressed against the cold steel, breathing slow. Below us, a barge moved without lights, loaded with something covered in black cloth. Grey Crow had warned me about these runs. I had not believed him — until now.
side:2.cnHint: 阿栗把我拉到桥的____，我们躲过了巡逻灯，看到了一艘秘密运货的船。
side:2.hook: The barge stopped directly below Zero's tower.
side:2.line: 'Stay on this *side* — the cameras do not reach here.'

air:2.en: The moment I stepped into the abandoned broadcast tower, the *air* changed. It tasted of old static and something sharper — a live signal, running hot. Grey Crow had said this tower went dark in 2091. It had not. Someone had kept it breathing, hidden inside the silence. I pressed my ear to the wall and listened.
air:2.cnHint: 我进入废弃的广播塔，发现____中有一种异常气息，暗示这里仍有活跃信号。
air:2.hook: The signal was broadcasting my name, on repeat.
air:2.line: 'Feel the *air* in here — that means the transmitter never stopped.'

consumption:2.en: The report Ali decoded was brutal in its plainness. Harbor City's power grid showed unusual *consumption* — massive draws from three points on the east grid, every night at exactly 02:00. Someone was running something enormous in the dark. Grey Crow circled the three points on the map. They formed a perfect triangle around my apartment.
consumption:2.cnHint: 解码报告显示电网的____数据异常，三个高耗电点围绕着我的公寓形成三角形。
consumption:2.hook: Tonight was the night the triangle would close.
consumption:2.line: 'That level of *consumption* means a machine the size of this room, running every night.'

field:2.en: The old sports *field* behind Grid Station Nine was dark, fenced off since the city banned public gatherings. Ali crouched near the gate, scanning a scratched metal plate bolted to the chain-link. Seven symbols. Not random. A map. I felt the signal pulse beneath my boots like a buried heartbeat.
field:2.cnHint: 阿栗在废弃的____后方发现了一块刻有神秘符号的金属板。
field:2.hook: The seventh symbol was still warm to the touch.
field:2.line: 'This *field* was sealed the same night the grid went dark,' Ali said.

personality:2.en: Grey Crow left a voice chip tucked inside a cracked junction box on Level B. I pressed play. The voice was flat, careful — stripped of any *personality* on purpose. But one word choice gave it away: 'observe,' not 'watch.' Grey Crow always said observe. My pulse jumped.
personality:2.cnHint: 灰鸦留下的声音芯片刻意掩盖了说话者的____，但一个词语出卖了他。
personality:2.hook: Someone else had already listened — the chip was still warm.
personality:2.line: 'Strip your *personality* out of every message you send,' Grey Crow had warned me once.

size:2.en: The data card Ali slid under my door was the *size* of a fingernail. I almost swept it off the desk. Printed on one face in ink too fine to read without a lens: a single frequency number. I pulled out my scanner. The number matched a banned broadcast channel.
size:2.cnHint: 阿栗送来的数据卡小得像指甲盖，却藏着一个被禁播的____频率编号。
size:2.hook: The frequency had gone silent exactly forty minutes ago.
size:2.line: 'Do not judge it by *size*,' Ali said. 'It carries everything.'

schedule:2.en: Pinned to the inside of the fuse panel was a folded paper *schedule* — handwritten, eight time slots, each paired with a grid sector. Tonight's slot was circled in red: Sector Four, 02:00. I checked my watch. Forty minutes left. Zero had been here and left this as a trap or a gift. I could not tell which.
schedule:2.cnHint: 保险盒内贴着一张手写的____，今晚的时间槽被红笔圈出。
schedule:2.hook: Only one person in the city still wrote in that handwriting.
schedule:2.line: 'Follow the *schedule* exactly,' the note beneath it read, 'or the signal dies.'

towards:2.en: I watched the shadow move *towards* the broken relay tower at the edge of the lower dock. It stopped once, turned, and I was certain it checked whether I was following. The figure wore Grey Crow's coat — or something made to look like it. Ali grabbed my arm before I could step forward.
towards:2.cnHint: 一个身影朝着废弃的中继塔____走去，似乎在确认有没有人跟随。
towards:2.hook: Ali's grip was tight enough to bruise.
towards:2.line: 'Walking *towards* that tower alone is exactly what Zero wants you to do.'

background:2.en: The image Zero broadcast on every dead screen in the sub-level showed only static — except for a faint *background* detail in the lower-left corner: a partial street sign, blue, with two visible letters. Ali froze the frame. I leaned in. That sign only existed in one block of Harbor City.
background:2.cnHint: 零点播出的静态画面中，____里隐藏着一个街道路牌的局部细节。
background:2.hook: That block had been officially listed as demolished three years ago.
background:2.line: 'Check the *background*,' Ali said quietly. 'Zero always hides the truth there.'

department:2.en: The stamp on the envelope read City Signal *Department*, Sector Nine — but that office had been closed for two years. Inside: a single key, no note. Someone was using a dead agency's name to move things through the city unquestioned. Grey Crow had warned me this would happen. I had not believed him.
department:2.cnHint: 信封上盖着一个早已关闭的____的印章，里面只有一把没有说明的钥匙。
department:2.hook: The key was cut for a lock I had seen only once before.
department:2.line: 'A dead *department* is the perfect cover,' Grey Crow said. 'No one checks a ghost.'

detail:2.en: Grey Crow's sketch of the server room looked rough at first glance, but every *detail* was precise: the height of the cable tray, the angle of the vent, the one unlocked panel marked with a small cross. He had been inside. Recently. I traced the cross with my finger and felt a cold certainty settle in my chest.
detail:2.cnHint: 灰鸦的草图看似粗糙，但每个____都极为准确，说明他不久前亲身去过。
detail:2.hook: The cross was drawn in the same ink as the anonymous warning I had received that morning.
detail:2.line: 'Every *detail* in that sketch is a message,' Grey Crow told me. 'Read them in order.'

indeed:2.en: The old server room smelled of burnt wire. I pushed open the cold metal door and found a small data chip taped to the back of a broken screen. Grey Crow had told me to search here. The chip was *indeed* real — warm, as if someone had just left it.
indeed:2.cnHint: 我在废弃服务器间找到了一枚芯片，它____是真实存在的。
indeed:2.hook: The chip pulsed once, then went dark in my hand.
indeed:2.line: 'It is *indeed* here — but who left it for us?'

launch:2.en: Ali slid a cracked tablet across the wet floor toward me. On the screen, a single countdown timer read four minutes. 'This is the *launch* signal,' she whispered. Outside, the harbour lights cut off one by one, and the whole city held its breath in the sudden dark.
launch:2.cnHint: 阿栗发现了一个倒计时，那是某次____的信号。
launch:2.hook: Three minutes left, and none of us knew what was coming.
launch:2.line: 'The *launch* starts in three minutes — we cannot stop it now.'

refer:2.en: I found a torn page pinned to a rusted pipe in the lower tunnels. Strange symbols covered it. Grey Crow had told me to *refer* to the old city grid map if I ever found marks like these. I unfolded the map with shaking hands and matched the first symbol.
refer:2.cnHint: 我在隧道里发现了神秘符号，必须____旧地图才能解读。
refer:2.hook: The last symbol on the page was my own name.
refer:2.line: '*Refer* to the map now — every second we wait costs us.'

trust:2.en: Ali pressed a small key into my palm and closed my fingers around it. She said nothing for a moment, just looked at me through the rain-streaked glass. In Harbor City, *trust* was rarer than clean air. I gripped the key and nodded, hoping I was not making a mistake.
trust:2.cnHint: 阿栗把钥匙交给我，这份____在这座城市里比什么都珍贵。
trust:2.hook: Behind her, a shadow moved that she could not see.
trust:2.line: '*Trust* me this once — I have never lied to you.'

discussion:2.en: Zero left a voice message on the dead channel, calm and almost polite. 'I think a *discussion* is overdue,' the voice said. A single image file was attached: a photo of me, taken an hour ago, in a place I had told no one about. He had been watching the whole time.
discussion:2.cnHint: 零点留下语音消息，说早该有一次____了，还附上了一张照片。
discussion:2.hook: In the photo, someone stood just behind me in the dark.
discussion:2.line: 'A *discussion* between us is long overdue, don't you think?'

extremely:2.en: The signal in the east tower was *extremely* weak — one bar, flickering. I pressed the receiver to my ear and caught three words before the static swallowed everything. Three words were enough. Grey Crow's voice had been steady, but I heard the fear underneath it, cold and deep.
extremely:2.cnHint: 东塔的信号____微弱，我只捕捉到了三个关键词。
extremely:2.hook: Those three words changed everything I thought I knew.
extremely:2.line: 'The noise is *extremely* close — cut the signal now.'

organize:2.en: Someone had used red tape to *organize* the scattered documents into neat rows on the floor of the empty shop. Each row was a different date. The earliest was ten years ago. The latest was tomorrow. I crouched down and read the top sheet. My unit was listed as the target.
organize:2.cnHint: 废弃店铺里，有人____了文件，最新日期竟是明天。
organize:2.hook: My own name appeared at the bottom of the final page.
organize:2.line: 'They *organize* everything — they planned this long before we arrived.'

pattern:2.en: I spread the intercepted messages on the wet ground and stepped back to see them whole. Ali pointed first. 'There,' she said. A *pattern* was forming — the same four code words, repeating every third message, like a heartbeat. Someone was sending a hidden signal inside the city's dead-air broadcast.
pattern:2.cnHint: 我们把截获的信息铺开，发现了一个隐藏的____。
pattern:2.hook: The pattern pointed straight to the police broadcast tower.
pattern:2.line: 'This *pattern* did not appear by chance — someone built it.'

attack:2.en: The old server room under Pier 7 smelled of rust and salt water. I found Ali crouched behind a dead terminal, breathing hard. 'Someone launched an *attack* on the grid at midnight,' she said. Every screen in the block had gone black. The silence felt like a held breath.
attack:2.cnHint: 阿栗告诉我，有人在午夜对电网发动了____，整片区域陷入黑暗。
attack:2.hook: But the real target was never the grid.
attack:2.line: 'Someone launched an *attack* on the grid — and we were meant to find this room.'

heavy:2.en: Grey Crow handed me a steel case without a word. I nearly dropped it. The thing was *heavy* — far too heavy for what he claimed were just data chips. I set it on the wet floor of the tunnel and stared at the lock. Three digits. I had one guess before it would seal forever.
heavy:2.cnHint: 灰鸦交给我一个出奇____的箱子，里面装的东西远不止他说的那样简单。
heavy:2.hook: The number I needed was hidden in a dead man's coat.
heavy:2.line: 'It's *heavy* because the truth always costs more than you expect.'

thought:2.en: I stood at the broken window of Sub-level 4 and looked down at the flooded street below. One *thought* kept circling in my mind: the blackout was not an accident. Someone had planned it, step by step, weeks before the city even felt the first flicker. I needed to find that plan.
thought:2.cnHint: 站在积水的街道上方，一个____在我脑海中不断盘旋：这次断电绝非意外。
thought:2.hook: The plan, I would learn, had my name in it.
thought:2.line: 'One *thought* is enough to change a city — if the right person thinks it.'

attract:2.en: Ali pressed a small silver disc to the wall near the old market gate. 'It will *attract* any active signal within fifty meters,' she whispered. We waited. The disc began to hum, low and steady. A line of blue light crept across its surface, then stopped — pointing directly at the sealed door across the lane.
attract:2.cnHint: 阿栗用一个装置来____附近的信号，结果蓝光径直指向了对面那扇封闭的门。
attract:2.hook: Someone behind that door was already listening to us.
attract:2.line: 'Place it here — it will *attract* the signal we have been chasing all night.'

define:2.en: Zero's voice came through the broken speaker like static shaped into words. 'You cannot *define* me by what I destroy,' he said. 'Look at what I build.' On the wall behind the speaker, fresh code was painted in glowing ink — a map of every power line in Harbor City, each one marked with a time.
define:2.cnHint: 零点声称我们无法用他的破坏行为来____他，并在墙上留下了一张带有时间标记的电力线路图。
define:2.hook: Every time on that map matched a future date.
define:2.line: 'You cannot *define* a person by one night, investigator — not even yourself.'

executive:2.en: A hard-copy memo lay in a puddle just inside the checkpoint door. The name at the top read: Regional *Executive*, Harbor City Power Bureau. Half the text was burned away. What remained listed six names — mine was the last one, added in different ink, as if by a different hand, long after the rest.
executive:2.cnHint: 一份备忘录上列着六个名字，最后一个是我的，而签发人是港城电力局的____。
executive:2.hook: I did not remember signing anything for the Power Bureau.
executive:2.line: 'The *executive* signed this order three weeks ago — long before the lights went out.'

expectation:2.en: Grey Crow met me at the top of the parking structure and said nothing for a long moment. Then: 'You found more than I sent you to find.' I nodded. His *expectation* had been a simple data pull — in and out in ten minutes. Instead I had a burned memo, a steel case, and a name I did not want to carry.
expectation:2.cnHint: 灰鸦原本对我的____只是简单取数据，没想到我带回来的东西让他沉默了很久。
expectation:2.hook: He looked at the memo and his jaw went tight.
expectation:2.line: 'My *expectation* was one file — you have brought me a reason to run.'

friendly:2.en: The woman behind the glass at the emergency relay post gave me a *friendly* nod — too easy, too warm for a city that had just lost all its lights. I slid the memo under the glass anyway. Her smile did not move. Her eyes, though, dropped to the burned name at the top and stayed there far too long.
friendly:2.cnHint: 中继站的女人对我表现得异常____，但当她看到备忘录上那个名字时，笑容却一动不动。
friendly:2.hook: She reached under the counter before I could step back.
friendly:2.line: 'I try to stay *friendly*, investigator — it makes people show me things they should keep hidden.'

transform:2.en: The old signal tower stood dark. I found a dial hidden behind a loose brick. One turn — static *transformed* into a voice, cold and clear: 'Slot Seven is open.' The whole room seemed to shift around me, walls catching faint blue light from a source I could not name.
transform:2.cnHint: 我在废弃的信号塔里转动一个旋钮，周围的一切瞬间____了。
transform:2.hook: The voice knew my name before I spoke it.
transform:2.line: 'One signal can *transform* a dead city into a living trap,' Grey Crow said.

additional:2.en: Ali slid a data chip across the wet table. 'Base file is clean,' she said. 'But there is *additional* code buried at the end — seven lines, invisible to standard scanners.' I plugged it in. The screen filled with names: every name on it was already dead.
additional:2.cnHint: 阿里发现芯片末尾藏有____的隐藏代码，那些名字令我心惊。
additional:2.hook: My own name appeared at the very bottom.
additional:2.line: 'There is *additional* data here — someone did not want us to find it,' Ali said.

journal:2.en: Behind the broken vending machine I found a water-stained *journal*. Each entry was dated, each page filled with short coded lines. The last entry read: 'Night 40. They are listening through the lights.' The ink was still faintly wet.
journal:2.cnHint: 我在破损的售货机后面发现了一本____，最后一页的墨迹未干。
journal:2.hook: The handwriting matched Grey Crow's exactly.
journal:2.line: 'This *journal* is the only record that Zero ever made a mistake,' Grey Crow said quietly.

sort:2.en: Zero left no obvious clues — that was the usual *sort* of move from someone who had been hiding for years. But Ali noticed the dust pattern on the shelf. Every item had been replaced in the wrong order, just by a centimetre. Someone had searched this room in a hurry.
sort:2.cnHint: 零点惯用这____手法掩盖行踪，但阿里从灰尘的痕迹中看出了破绽。
sort:2.hook: The shelf held one item that did not belong here.
sort:2.line: 'I know every *sort* of trick Zero uses — this one is new,' Ali said.

understanding:2.en: Grey Crow handed me a folded map covered in tiny symbols. 'Your *understanding* of this city is still shallow,' he said. 'These marks show where the signal dies — and where it is killed on purpose.' I stared at the crosses. They formed a near-perfect ring around my apartment block.
understanding:2.cnHint: 灰鸦说我对这座城市的____还太浅，地图上的标记让我背脊发凉。
understanding:2.hook: The ring was tightening one block per night.
understanding:2.line: 'Your *understanding* of what Zero wants is the only thing keeping you alive,' Grey Crow said.

citizen:2.en: The notice board near the flooded underpass was plastered with city alerts. One poster read: 'Every *citizen* must register a voice print by dawn.' Below the official text, in tiny scratched letters, someone had added: 'Do not comply.' A small red crow was drawn beside the warning.
citizen:2.cnHint: 公告栏上要求每位____在黎明前完成声纹登记，但下方有人留下了反抗的字句。
citizen:2.hook: The scratched letters were still warm to the touch.
citizen:2.line: 'A *citizen* who registers tonight hands Zero the last key it needs,' Grey Crow warned.

contrast:2.en: Two photographs lay side by side on the evidence shelf. The first showed Harbor City ten years ago — open sky, dry streets, people without masks. The *contrast* with today's image was sharp enough to cut: the same street, now roofed in black cable, every face hidden. Something had been erased from the skyline.
contrast:2.cnHint: 两张照片的____触目惊心——十年前的天空与如今的黑缆丛林判若云泥，天际线上有东西消失了。
contrast:2.hook: The missing building had been replaced with a listening station.
contrast:2.line: 'Look at the *contrast* — that is the night Zero first took control,' Ali said.

establish:2.en: Ali spread the circuit diagram flat. 'Zero did not just cut the power,' she said. 'It used the blackout to *establish* a private relay — invisible, citywide, already active.' I traced the lines with one finger. Every hospital, every school, every shelter fed into a single dark node at the harbour.
establish:2.cnHint: 阿里发现零点借助断电在全市____了一个秘密中继网络，核心节点就在港口。
establish:2.hook: The node had been transmitting for exactly three hours.
establish:2.line: 'We have minutes to destroy it before Zero can *establish* full control,' Ali said.

estimate:2.en: The dead server room smelled of burnt wire. Grey Crow handed me a cracked data chip. 'My *estimate* puts the blackout at eighteen hours old,' he said, voice flat. That meant whoever killed the grid had a full night to vanish. The trail was already cold.
estimate:2.cnHint: 格雷·克劳根据残留热量对停电时间做出了____，线索已经变得冰冷。
estimate:2.hook: Eighteen hours was enough time to erase everything.
estimate:2.line: 'My *estimate* puts us eighteen hours behind, and that gap is growing.'

explore:2.en: Ali pressed her ear against the sealed vault door. 'We need to *explore* the lower level before backup power dies,' she whispered. I checked the timer — four minutes left. The elevator was dead. Only a rusted service ladder dropped into the dark below, swaying slightly in air that should not have been moving.
explore:2.cnHint: 阿里提议____地下层，但梯子在不该有风的地方轻轻摇晃。
explore:2.hook: Something below us was already breathing.
explore:2.line: 'We have to *explore* that lower level before the lights die for good.'

fix:2.en: Zero had nailed a single playing card to the relay tower door — a message only I could read. The card gave me a *fix* on his position: Pier Nine, east docks. Grey Crow said nothing. He just turned up his collar against the rain and started walking. That silence scared me more than any threat.
fix:2.cnHint: 那张扑克牌给了我零的____，格雷·克劳的沉默令我不安。
fix:2.hook: Grey Crow already knew where the card would lead us.
fix:2.line: 'That card is a *fix* — he wants you to walk straight into his range.'

general:2.en: The broadcast was not aimed at one person. Ali translated the static: a *general* warning, pushed to every receiver in Harbor City at once. Someone wanted the whole grid to know the blackout was not an accident. I felt the crowd on the street slow down, heads lifting, faces pale under the neon.
general:2.cnHint: 阿里翻译出那段静电噪音是一条面向____大众的警告广播。
general:2.hook: A city that knows it was targeted is a city about to panic.
general:2.line: 'This is a *general* alert — whoever sent it wants everyone afraid tonight.'

loss:2.en: Grey Crow spread the stolen ledger across the hood of a dead taxi. Column after column showed a *loss* — data sectors wiped, not stolen, just gone. 'They weren't after profit,' he said. I stared at the numbers. Destroying information this clean cost more than taking it. That made our enemy patient, and rich.
loss:2.cnHint: 账本上一列列的____显示数据被彻底抹除，而非窃走。
loss:2.hook: Only one kind of enemy destroys what they could sell.
loss:2.line: 'Every entry shows a *loss* — they paid a fortune just to leave nothing behind.'

partner:2.en: Ali grabbed my sleeve at the top of the fire escape. 'I am your *partner*, not your shield,' she said sharply. Below us, Zero's drones swept the alley in slow arcs of blue light. I had been about to step in front of her. She was right. We moved together into the shadow, silent.
partner:2.cnHint: 阿里提醒我她是我的____，不是用来挡在身前的盾牌。
partner:2.hook: Moving as one was the only way either of us survived the night.
partner:2.line: 'I am your *partner* — stop treating me like someone you need to protect.'

concept:2.en: Zero had left a single sentence burned into the relay panel: FREEDOM IS A *CONCEPT* THEY SELL BACK TO YOU. Grey Crow photographed it without a word. I stood in the flicker of dying lights, reading it again. It was graffiti, yes — but the encryption tag beneath it matched a signal we had traced for months.
concept:2.cnHint: 零在中继面板上烧刻的句子里出现了一个____，其下的加密标记让我们追查已久。
concept:2.hook: The tag meant Zero had been inside this building before we were born.
concept:2.line: 'The *concept* he burned here is a signature — he wants us to understand him.'

history:2.en: The archive terminal was still warm. Someone had pulled the city's full infrastructure *history* — every blackout, every repair, every hidden override code going back sixty years. Grey Crow knelt and read the access log. One user. Thirty seconds. They had what they needed before we even knew the power was gone.
history:2.cnHint: 有人在停电前抢先调取了城市基础设施的全部____记录。
history:2.hook: Sixty years of secrets downloaded in thirty seconds flat.
history:2.line: 'They pulled the entire *history* — they know every weakness this city has ever had.'

manage:0.en: The city grid died at midnight. Every screen went black. I sat in the server room, hands shaking, cables tangled around my boots. Grey Crow had left one instruction: keep the backup node alive. Somehow, through the dark and the noise, I *managed* to restart it before Zero's signal reached the core.
manage:0.cnHint: 断电之夜，叙述者在服务器室里____保住了备用节点，阻止了零点的信号入侵。
manage:0.hook: But the node was already sending data — somewhere I did not know.
manage:0.line: 'I don\'t know how you *managed* it, but Zero is watching you now.'

forget:1.en: The blackout hit Harbor City at midnight. Every screen went dark. I stood on Neon Row, rain soaking my coat, staring at the spot where Grey Crow had told me to wait. But I could not *forget* the warning he had whispered: 'When the lights die, the real signals begin.'
forget:1.cnHint: 停电的那一刻，叙述者站在霓虹街上，脑海中挥不去灰鸦的____。
forget:1.hook: Something moved in the dark where nothing should move.
forget:1.line: 'Don't *forget* — the signal comes once, and only once.'

national:2.en: The power grid died at midnight. In the sudden dark, my scanner picked up a faint signal bleeding from a cracked wall panel — a *national* emergency broadcast, hidden beneath dead static, meant for every city in the country at once. Someone had buried it here weeks ago.
national:2.cnHint: 停电后，叙述者在墙板里发现了一条被压制的____紧急广播信号。
national:2.hook: The signal carried a date: three days from now.
national:2.line: 'This is a *national* alert — every city will hear it soon,' Grey Crow whispered.
